blocks.text: Condo buildings in Township of Langley Plans

This page is NOT a listing feed: at reading it carried no MLS® listing cards and no result count — it is a Township of Langley land-use plans index, a short intro plus twelve tappable plan tiles linking to tol.ca. There is therefore no in-area condo stock to count for this page. CONFLICT FLAGGED: five tiles state as completed fact that their plans were "repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026" and replaced by Bylaw No. 6202 or 6203, but the Township's own Willoughby Community Plan Update page records only first and second reading of Bylaw Nos. 6201, 6202 and 6203 on May 25, 2026, with a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026 — no adoption is recorded on any Township source opened.

items.t: The page's scope: browser title "Township of Langley Land Use Plans, OCP Maps & Zoning Updates," covering the whole Township of Langley through twelve plan tiles — Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Carvolth, Central Gordon Estate, Jericho, Latimer, Murrayville, North East Gordon Estate, Routley, Smith, Walnut Grove, Williams, Yorkson — each summarizing a community or neighbourhood plan and linking to tol.ca.
Board geography: there is no board sub-area for this topic; the page covers the whole Township.

Where condo stock concentrates under these plans: this page names no buildings, so no concentration is stated from it. As plan context only, the Township's own Willoughby update frames Willoughby as the Township's urban growth area expected to accommodate a significant portion of future population growth, with TransLink's proposed bus rapid transit service along 200 Street as a key driver and a new transit-oriented-development Development Permit Area proposed — plan policy, not a building count.

Planning structure, in the Township's own description: Township community planning is guided by the Sustainability Charter, and "The Official Community Plan and component Community and Neighbourhood Plans help make the vision a reality by providing policies and actions specific to each area"; the Community and Policy Planning division also owns functional plans including the Agricultural Viability Strategy, Climate Action Strategy, Heritage Strategy and Fraser Highway Employment Lands Area Plan.

One plan-level school fact is recorded in the Township's Gordon Neighbourhood Plan draft: Bylaw No. 6203's plan area includes Langley Fire Hall No. 4 and a daycare and learning centre among its key institutional uses — a draft-plan statement, with the bylaw itself at reading stage only.

items.t: The Township plan stack, cited exactly as verified: the Official Community Plan is given effect through Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842 as amended; in 2025 the Township completed an OCP update to align with housing-related amendments to the Local Government Act, and on December 1, 2025 Council adopted the 2025 Official Community Plan Update Bylaw No. 6200 (as amended). The December 2025 update set included the Aldergrove, Murrayville, Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Northwest Langley community plans and the Yorkson, Smith and Williams Neighbourhood Plans.

Willoughby Community Plan — origin and current schedule, per standing correction: the Willoughby Community Plan originates as Bylaw 1836 (1979) and now sits as Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025). The Township's 2026 update package proposes a new Willoughby Community Plan (Bylaw No. 6201), a Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202, consolidating the Carvolth, Latimer, Jericho, Routley and Southwest Gordon Estate neighbourhood plans) and a Gordon Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6203, consolidating the Central Gordon Estate and Northeast Gordon Estate neighbourhood plans), plus a new transit-oriented-development Development Permit Area. Status, exactly as the Township records it: Council gave first and second reading to Bylaw Nos.

Murrayville Community Plan (verified at bylaw level): Bylaw 1988 No. 2661, adopted April 17, 1989 as an amendment to the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842, since amended including by the 2025 OCP Update (Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025); the plan describes Murrayville on both sides of the Fraser Highway immediately east of the City of Langley.

Zoning and SSMUH (Township): zoning is under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 as amended. The SSMUH amendments are Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024 — 3 units on eligible lots at ≤280 m² and 4 units at 280–4,050 m², with NO 6-plex tier — and on April 27, 2026 Council adopted Schedule 4 of the OCP implementing a Development Permit Area with form and character guidelines for SSMUH. The Township suite cap is 120 m². SSMUH eligibility turns on Urban Containment Boundary, municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit-Oriented Area, and ≤4,050 m². The Township's one Transit-Oriented Area is on 196 Street in Willowbrook for the proposed Surrey-Langley SkyTrain station, designated by provincial Order-in-Council on May 2, 2025, with minimum allowable densities of 8–20 storeys within 800 m depending on proximity.

blocks.text: Good to know about Township of Langley Plans

items.t: The page's June 15, 2026 "repeal" date is the hearing date in the Township's own record.
Five tiles are affected, and they are named.

The Gordon plan area's boundaries are in the draft, even though the bylaw is not adopted. Bylaw No. 6203's draft plan places the Gordon neighbourhood in southeast Willoughby, bounded by 73A and 72 Avenues and north of Crush Crescent to the ALR boundary, the Willowbrook Connector and ALR boundary to the east, 68 and 66A Avenues to the south, and 206 and 202B Street to the west — useful for identifying whether a parcel is even in the draft area, without treating the draft as law.

Brookswood-Fernridge is still being refined lot-by-lot. The Rinn Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6010, adopted June 10, 2024) already has a Rinn Update 2026 (Bylaw No. 6219) recorded May 25, 2026 — in this area the neighbourhood plan, not just the community plan, is the document to check before pricing a parcel.

The December 2025 update already changed more than the tiles suggest. The Bylaw No. 6200 update set (adopted December 1, 2025) included not only the OCP but the Aldergrove, Murrayville, Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Northwest Langley community plans and the Yorkson, Smith and Williams neighbourhood plans — a parcel in any of those areas is under a December 2025 plan version even if its tile looks unchanged.
Site copy on the tiles is not verified plan content.

Two municipalities named Langley share one market row. The SnapStats Langley community figures in combine the Township and the City of Langley — a Township parcel's plan position cannot be read off a combined City-plus-Township median, and the City's bylaws are a separate check from everything in.

items.t: What the page actually is: plan tiles only — community-plan tiles (Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Murrayville, Walnut Grove, plus the Willoughby frame in its neighbourhood tiles) and the Willoughby neighbourhood-plan set (Carvolth, Central Gordon Estate, Jericho, Latimer, North East Gordon Estate, Routley, Smith, Williams, Yorkson), each linking to tol.ca — with no listing cards to characterize. The tile-count inconsistency ("twelve tiles," thirteen names listed) is flagged in the status block.

The plan stack a Township parcel can sit under (the land-relevant content of this topic): the Official Community Plan (as updated by Bylaw No. 6200, Dec 1, 2025), a community plan, a neighbourhood plan where one exists, Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (as amended, including SSMUH Bylaw No. 6020), and Development Permit Areas such as the SSMUH DPA adopted April 27, 2026. A plan designation is policy, not serviced lots and not for-sale stock.

Verified plan anchors: the Murrayville Community Plan is Bylaw 1988 No. 2661, adopted April 17, 1989 as an amendment to the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842, since amended including by the 2025 OCP Update (Bylaw No. 6200); the Rinn Neighbourhood Plan is Bylaw No. 6010 within the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan (Bylaw 2017 No. 5300), adopted June 10, 2024, with a Rinn Update 2026 (Bylaw No. 6219) recorded May 25, 2026.
Assemblies / proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: Bylaw Nos.

items.t: OCP / plans — Township: the 2025 OCP Update, Bylaw No. 6200, was adopted December 1, 2025; the December 2025 update set included the Aldergrove, Murrayville, Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Northwest Langley community plans and the Yorkson, Smith and Williams Neighbourhood Plans. The Willoughby Community Plan's origin bylaw 1836 now sits as Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200. Bylaws 6201/6202/6203: first/second reading May 25, 2026 ONLY, Public Hearing directed June 15, 2026 — never upgraded.

ALR block (where ALR ground exists in the Township — parcel-specific): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

items.t: June 15, 2026 was a hearing date, not a repeal date (Township record, read Nov 1, 2026). The Township's Willoughby update page records first and second reading of Bylaw Nos.
The Murrayville plan is from 1989 and still live. Bylaw No. 2661 (adopted April 17, 1989) as amended by the 2025 OCP Update — read the current consolidated version, not the 1989 text alone.

Rinn is still being refined lot by lot. The Rinn Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6010, adopted June 10, 2024) already has a Rinn Update 2026 (Bylaw No. 6219) recorded May 25, 2026 — in Brookswood-Fernridge the neighbourhood plan, not just the community plan, drives a parcel.

faq.q: Have the Carvolth, Jericho, Latimer, Routley and Gordon Estate plans been repealed?
faq.a: 6202/6203, but the Township's Willoughby update page records only first and second reading of Bylaw Nos. 6201, 6202 and 6203 on May 25, 2026, with a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026 — June 15, 2026 is the hearing date in the Township record, not a recorded repeal date. Confirm adoption with the Township before relying on either version.

faq.q: How do I read a Township parcel before offering?
faq.a: In layers, in this order: OCP designation (Bylaw No. 6200 update, December 1, 2025), then the community plan, then any neighbourhood plan, then current zoning under Bylaw No. 2500 — the plan shows where the Township wants growth; the zoning is what can be built as-of-right today.

faq.q: What is the Willoughby plan, in one line?
faq.a: A community plan originating as Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025), with a 2026 update package (Bylaws 6201–6203) at first/second reading as of May 25, 2026 — the existing plan, as amended in December 2025, is the governing version on every source opened.

faq.q: Which bylaw is the Willoughby Community Plan?
faq.a: Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025).

faq.q: How do I read a Township parcel's potential?
faq.a: In layers: OCP designation (Bylaw No. 6200 update, Dec 1, 2025), then the community plan, then any neighbourhood plan, then current zoning under Bylaw No. 2500 — the plan shows where the Township wants growth; the zoning is what can be built as-of-right today.

faq.q: Have the Carvolth, Jericho, Latimer, Routley and Gordon Estate plans been repealed?
faq.a: 6202/6203, but Township records support only first and second reading on May 25, 2026 with a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026 — confirm adoption with the Township before relying on the repeal.

faq.q: What is the Willoughby Plan's current bylaw home?
faq.a: Origin Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted Dec 1, 2025).

faq.q: Does a plan designation mean I can subdivide?
faq.a: No — designation is policy. Subdivision needs Approving Officer approval, and servicing is governed by the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw 2019 No. 5382; ALR parcels also need ALC approval to subdivide.

faq.q: What is the Township of Langley's Official Community Plan?
faq.a: The Township's long-range policy plan, given effect through the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842 as amended — most recently by the 2025 OCP Update, Bylaw No. 6200, adopted December 1, 2025 — with component Community and Neighbourhood Plans providing area-specific policies under it

faq.q: Is this page a listing page?
faq.a: No: at reading it carried no MLS® listings or result count — it is an index of twelve Township community and neighbourhood plan tiles linking to tol.ca, covering Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Willoughby, Murrayville and Walnut Grove among others

faq.q: How do the community plans interact with SSMUH?
faq.a: The plans set area policy while the zoning amendments do the permitting: Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units at ≤280 m² and 4 units at 280–4,050 m² on eligible lots, and an OCP Schedule 4 Development Permit Area for SSMUH form and character was adopted April 27, 2026
